content: Upper respiratory tract infection (URTI) refers to an illness caused by an acute infection that affects the upper respiratory tract, including the nose, sinuses, pharynx, or larynx. In the United States, there are approximately one billion cases of acute upper respiratory illnesses annually. About 15% of acute pharyngitis cases are attributed to bacterial infections, most commonly caused by Group A Streptococcus, also known as strep throat. Patients with strep throat typically present with a sore throat as their initial symptom. Unlike viral upper respiratory infections, they generally do not experience symptoms such as a runny nose, cough, or sneezing. Epidemiologically, upper respiratory tract infections are among the most common illnesses caused by acute infections involving the upper respiratory tract. In the United States alone, these infections account for roughly one billion cases each year. While anyone can contract the common cold, certain populations are at higher risk. These include children, elderly individuals, and those with compromised immune systems, who are more frequently affected by such infections.
